case_title: Achhar Singh v. State of Himachal Pradesh
accused_victim_relationship: Neighbour (Budhi Singh, per the judgment); Achhar Singh is described only as a villager, with no stated relationship to the victims
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 (Budhi Singh); IPC ss.326, 323 and 452 (Achhar Singh); IPC s.452 (Budhi Singh); other charged sections 147, 148, 506 IPC
weapon: Axe (other accused had sickles, spears and sticks; stones were also thrown)
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony; medical evidence (post-mortem and injury reports); recovery evidence (axe, blood-stained articles, door and bulb pieces); FIR; independent recovery witness
aggravating_circumstances: Axe blow to the head of an elderly woman, a vital body part; accused broke open the door and entered the house armed
trial_court_outcome: All accused acquitted by the Additional Sessions Judge, Mandi, giving benefit of doubt
high_court_outcome: Acquittal of Budhi Singh and Achhar Singh set aside; convicted (Budhi Singh under ss.302 and 452 IPC; Achhar Singh under ss.452, 326 and 323 IPC); acquittal of the other five accused upheld
offence_finally_established: Budhi Singh: murder (IPC s.302) and house trespass (IPC s.452); Achhar Singh: house trespass (IPC s.452), voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons (IPC s.326) and voluntarily causing hurt (IPC s.323)
neutral_facts: On the night of the incident, the victim's family had returned from a wedding feast in a nearby village and were eating their meal at home. Around 8 pm, several villagers, including the accused, called out for the complainant and his father to come outside. When they approached the door, they perceived an intent to kill and were pelted with stones, which prompted them to bolt the door. The assailants broke it open and entered the house armed: two of them carried axes, while others carried sickles, spears and sticks. One accused allegedly struck the elderly victim on the head with an axe, causing her death on the spot. Another accused allegedly struck the complainant's father with an axe, causing him to faint. The complainant was beaten with sticks and escaped to the roof. Some bystanders intervened and the attackers left. At about 2 am the complainant went to a village leader, who advised him to contact the police. Phone lines were down and no buses ran at night, so he walked about 24 km to a police station and lodged a complaint the next morning. Police recovered an axe, sticks, a blood-stained stone, glass splinters, broken door pieces, a broken bulb and leftover food from the house. An independent witness corroborated some of these recoveries. A post-mortem found one fatal head injury caused by a sharp-edged weapon, and the doctor said it could have been caused by the axe shown in evidence. The father's injuries were consistent with both sharp and blunt weapons. The complainant, his wife and his father consistently named the same two accused for the fatal blow and the axe attack. Seven persons were charge-sheeted.
physical_harm: Death of Swari Devi from one fatal head injury by a sharp-edged weapon; Beli Ram suffered incised wounds on face and back of skull, facial bone fracture and other injuries
number_of_offences: 7 charged; 4 finally upheld (IPC ss.302, 452, 326 and 323 across the two appellants)
financial_property_loss: Damage to door, windows and utensils (no monetary value stated)
premeditation_planning: Not stated; the High Court noted no common intention to kill or cause grievous hurt, and liability was individual
motive: alleged: prior animosity over the complainant's land and prior litigation; social boycott of the complainant's family by Budhi Singh and others
key_evidence_accepted: Consistent eyewitness testimony of P.W.1, P.W.11 and P.W.12 on the fatal axe blow by Budhi Singh and the axe attack by Achhar Singh; FIR; post-mortem and medical evidence; axe recovery; P.W.14 recovery corroboration
witness_credibility: Witnesses exaggerated injuries, but their core account of the fatal blow was consistent with the FIR and medical evidence; exaggeration was held distinct from falsity and the truth separable; the complainant's account was consistent from the FIR onward
bail_history: Not stated earlier; at the Supreme Court bail bonds were cancelled and the appellants directed to undergo the remainder of their sentence
trial_duration: offence: 23.02.1996 (night of incident); trial judgment: 24.02.1998; High Court: 12.05.2010 and 27.05.2010; Supreme Court: 07.05.2021
legal_representation: Accused (appellants): J.S. Attri and R. Basant, Sr. Advs., with Rameshwar Prasad Goyal, R. Anand Padmanabhan, Vishnu Pazhanganat and Shashi Bhushan Kumar, Advs. State: Abhinav Mukerji, AAG
investigation_status: FIR No. 36 of 1996 lodged 24.02.1996; police investigation completed; charge-sheet filed against seven of the sixteen named persons; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: all accused acquitted (24.02.1998). High Court: acquittal of two appellants set aside and convicted; acquittal of the other five upheld. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed, High Court convictions maintained
prosecution_argument: The FIR is not substantive evidence and may only be used against its maker; witnesses' credibility is not defeated by relationship or minor exaggerations; inconsistent evidence against one accused cannot benefit another (relying on Gangadhar Behera and Prabhu Dayal)
defence_argument: Witnesses exaggerate and falsely implicate; medical evidence shows only one head injury; the trial court's view was a possible view and interference required perversity; the axe was recovered from a public place; a blood trail outside the house; police arrival and time of death doubtful; no reason for Budhi Singh to fight on his daughter's wedding day; parity with Narinder Singh
legal_principle_applied: Presumption of innocence and the double presumption after acquittal; appellate power to re-appreciate evidence; perversity where the trial court ignored relevant material; exaggeration is distinct from falsity and the grain must be sifted from the chaff; benefit of doubt only when a firm conclusion cannot be reached
precedent_relied_upon: Babu v. State of Kerala (2010) 9 SCC 189; Hari Chand v. State of Delhi (1996) 9 SCC 112; Dalip Singh v. State of Punjab AIR 1953 SC 364; Sarwan Singh v. State of Punjab (1976) 4 SCC 369; Sucha Singh v. State of Punjab (2003) 7 SCC 643; Chandrappa v. State of Karnataka (2007) 4 SCC 415; State of AP v. M. Madhusudhan Rao (2008) 15 SCC 582; Woolmington v. DPP [1935] AC 462
judicial_aggravating_factors: Fatal axe blow to the head of an elderly woman, a vital body part, known to be likely to cause death
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds cancelled; appellants directed to undergo the remainder of their sentence
